scope: Selected contextual statements, not an exhaustive incident source or an event inclusion gate. Episode nodes are not added to UCDP death totals.

sources.title: UN Secretary-General briefing and member-state statements, 28 February 2026
UN Lebanon: escalation beginning 2 March; published 13 March 2026
Security Council S/PV.10189, 2 July 2026, pp. 2-5; Secretariat briefing and Bahrain statement

episodes.label: US-Israeli strikes in Iran
episodes.summary: The UN describes joint US-Israeli strikes in Iran. US and Israeli representatives frame their action in terms of threats and prevention.

episodes.label: Iranian strikes across region
episodes.summary: The UN describes Iran's regional strikes as retaliatory. Iran describes the opening strikes as aggression.

episodes.label: Hezbollah fire / Israeli response
episodes.summary: The UN Lebanon account dates the escalation to Hezbollah fire followed by Israeli retaliation. This is a linked theatre, not a new observation added to conflict 16905.

episodes.label: Commercial shipping struck
episodes.summary: The Secretariat describes two vessel strikes near Hormuz, attributing one to an Iranian drone; the IMO was reviewing that incident.

episodes.label: US strikes in Hormozgan
episodes.summary: US strikes on 26-27 June were described by the US as responding to shipping attacks. Iran called them a ceasefire violation.

episodes.label: Iranian Gulf strikes / US strikes
episodes.summary: Iran said it targeted US infrastructure in Kuwait and Bahrain; later US strikes followed. Bahrain characterized attacks as planned rather than spontaneous. That contests interpretation, not temporal association.

links.basis: shared actor and subsequent date; inferred theatre connection, not established trigger
chronological response-compatible sequence and reported statements

denial_note: No explicit denial of retaliatory motive was established in these selected sources. Preventive framing and Bahrain's planned-action claim are not rewritten as such a denial. Any future explicit denial can be recorded without removing its event or timing edges.
